subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw add a public plugin-SDK dreaming lifecycle/config contract for non-memory-core memory plugins, or keep generic dreaming orchestration outside core as plugin-owned ClawHub behavior?
rationale: The requested change adds durable plugin API, config, scheduler, and memory-state surface; current code has only a memory-core sidecar workaround, while an overlapping role-slot PR may change the appropriate contract shape.

options.title: Coordinate With Memory Role Slots
options.body: Use the open memory role-slot work as the foundation, then design a narrow dreaming lifecycle contract only after the role taxonomy is accepted.

options.title: Keep Dreaming Plugin-Owned
options.body: Document ClawHub packages as the extension path and avoid adding a core-managed dreaming provider protocol for now.

options.title: Prototype A Narrow SDK RFC
options.body: Ask for a smaller RFC or PR that defines the provider methods, config ownership, scheduler behavior, migration story, and proof requirements without broad memory-slot changes.

recommendation.title: Coordinate With Memory Role Slots
recommendation.body: Use the open memory role-slot work as the foundation, then design a narrow dreaming lifecycle contract only after the role taxonomy is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is product/API direction for core plugin and config surface, and current-main history points this owner at the relevant code context.
